actions.reason: RegexTokenizer.train now collapses identical regex chunks into one entry with an occurrence count, keeping the order in which each chunk first appears. Pair counting adds that count instead of 1, and each merge pass scans every distinct chunk once rather than every occurrence. A pair can only first appear in a chunk's first occurrence, so pairs enter the stats dict in the same order as before. That means max() breaks ties the same way, and the counts, merges and vocab are identical. Measured train_ir ratio 0.7054, equivalence outputs identical, all tests pass.

+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -60,8 +60,17 @@ class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
         num_merges = vocab_size - 256
 
         # split the text up into text chunks and encode them
-        ids = [chunk_ids for chunk in self.compiled_pattern.findall(text)
-            if len(chunk_ids := list(chunk.encode("utf-8"))) >= 2]
+        # identical chunks are kept once (in first-seen order) with a count
+        chunk_counts = {}

+            chunk_counts[chunk] = chunk_counts.get(chunk, 0) + 1
+        ids = []
+        counts = []
+        for chunk, count in chunk_counts.items():
+            chunk_ids = list(chunk.encode("utf-8"))
+            if len(chunk_ids) >= 2:
+                ids.append(chunk_ids)
+                counts.append(count)
 
         # iteratively merge the most common pairs to create new tokens
         merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
@@ -70,12 +79,12 @@ class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
             # count the number of times every consecutive pair appears
             stats = {}
             stats_get = stats.get
-            for chunk_ids in ids:
+            for chunk_ids, count in zip(ids, counts):
                 it = iter(chunk_ids)
                 prev = next(it)
                 for curr in it:
                     pair = (prev, curr)
-                    stats[pair] = stats_get(pair, 0) + 1
+                    stats[pair] = stats_get(pair, 0) + count
                     prev = curr
             # find the pair with the highest count
             pair = max(stats, key=stats.get)

journal.text:
I changed RegexTokenizer.train in minbpe/regex.py. Identical regex chunks are now collapsed into one entry with an occurrence count, kept in first-appearance order. Pair counting adds that count instead of 1. Each merge pass scans every distinct chunk once instead of every occurrence. The edits replaced lines 63-64 with 11 lines and lines 82-87 with 6 lines.

In my sandbox, train_ir went from 2538722280 to 1790725649, ratio 0.7054. encode_ir went from 1013783125 to 1014477496, ratio 1.0007, within guard limits. Outputs were identical. The guard passed on 1 file, 17 lines. I submitted it, and it is waiting on independent replays.

Training cost here is driven by repeated chunks. A pair can only first appear in a chunk's first occurrence, so stats insertion order and tie-breaking are unchanged. Encode was not touched.

Next, I would look at whether the merge pass can update counts only for chunks containing the merged pair, instead of rescanning all distinct chunks.
